exposure: sonographic features at initial diagnosis (exogenous implantation pattern, rich vascularity on color Doppler, embryonic cardiac activity detection)
cohort: The study included 27 patients with recurrent cesarean scar pregnancy matched 1:1 with 27 CSP patients who had normal subsequent pregnancies, selected from a larger cohort of 1371 confirmed CSP cases between 2012-2022.
finding: Recurrent cesarean scar pregnancy is characterized by distinct sonographic features at initial diagnosis, including an exogenous implantation pattern, rich vascular flow, and embryonic cardiac activity, and while transabdominal ultrasound-guided suction curettage is effective for initial management, patients still face long-term risks of recurrence and infertility.
